title: Journey Telescope: Correlation-ID Driven Drilldown & Timeline Prism
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and prototype a focused drilldown surface that centers around a single correlation ID (the 'Journey Telescope') and a compact, multi-scale timeline view (the 'Timeline Prism'). Goal is to let engineers rapidly understand causal sequences across services, surface key divergent branches, and jump to artifacts (logs/metrics/PRs) with minimal context switching.
goals: Provide a single-entry drilldown for correlation IDs that aggregates related requests across regions/services
Visualize causal forks and durations in a compressed, zoomable timeline to preserve scanning speed for long-lived sessions
Expose quick-actions: pin to dashboard, open strict time-window in logs, create a rerun/recording, and attach to rollout experiments
Keep the surface performant at 200+ spans and usable on mid-range laptops (design constraints)
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to see the end-to-end sequence for a correlation ID so I can identify where latency originated
As a PM, I want to bookmark a problematic session and attach it to a canary rollout to demonstrate regression
As an engineer, I want to filter a session down to error-bearing branches so I can triage without noise
constraints: Backend will provide pre-aggregated adjacency lists and per-span min/median/max durations; we cannot request full span payloads for large sessions in the first iteration
Design must reuse console visual primitives (chips, sidecar panels, timeline axis) to minimize engineering effort
Accessibility: keyboard navigation and color-safe palette for branching indicators
engineering_notes_for_handoff: Provide three rendering modes: compact (summary), expanded (per-span rows), and condensed (sparkline-only) toggles
Use progressive reveal for full span attributes: fetch on click to avoid initial payload bloat
Branch glyphs encode: green (success), amber (retry/warning), red (error), grey (unknown). Include pattern for aggregated sibling counts
Accessibility: include ARIA labels for timeline controls and an announced focus when jumping to a span
acceptance_criteria: Clickable correlation ID entry from search and request list opens Journey Telescope centered on that ID
Timeline Prism renders sessions up to 300 spans with p95 interactive latency < 200ms on mid-range hardware
Quick-actions panel exposes: open logs (time-windowed), pin session, create incident draft, link to related PR (if present)
Design reviewed and signed-off by PM and two engineers; prototype usability test (5 participants) shows median task completion < 90s for root-cause locate task
decision_log: 2026-02-23 — Chose correlation-ID centric entry vs. service-centric landing to reduce context switching (PM + Eng decision)
2026-02-26 — Use progressive fetch for full span metadata to meet payload constraints (Eng proposal accepted)
2026-03-03 — Prioritized compact mode first to support quick scanning; expanded mode deferred to next cycle
tradeoffs: Not showing full span payloads by default reduces payload but may require extra clicks for deep debugging
Compact encoding of branches sacrifices vertical fidelity for scan speed; team accepted this for initial rollout
Embedding quick-actions increases surface complexity but improves mean-time-to-ack; will monitor usage metrics
